business_problem: Amdocs needed to help telecom providers automate complex customer and network workflows with domain-specific AI while lowering inference cost and latency enough for near-real-time production use.
solution_summary: Amdocs built its amAIz platform on NVIDIA infrastructure to create telecom-specific generative AI agents for sales, billing, care, and network operations. NVIDIA DGX Cloud and NVIDIA AI Enterprise provide the training and enterprise AI foundation for commercially available and domain-adapted LLMs, while NVIDIA NIM microservices expose optimized inference endpoints and support frameworks such as NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang. Amdocs also built an LLMOps pipeline around the NVIDIA AI Blueprint for building data flywheels, combining NVIDIA NeMo microservices for fine-tuning, evaluation, and guardrailing with NVIDIA NIM for deployment. On top of that stack, Amdocs uses NVIDIA Nemotron and Llama Nemotron to power amAIz agents that can autonomously handle multistep telecom journeys and plug into AI factories as reusable production services.

data_flow: Telecom workflow context enters amAIz, DGX Cloud and NeMo-based data-flywheel pipelines adapt and guardrail domain models, NIM serves the resulting models and agents through optimized inference frameworks, and the agents return actions or responses for sales, billing, care, and network operations.
business_outcome: With NVIDIA NIM microservices and the surrounding telecom AI stack, Amdocs reduced token use by as much as 60 percent in preprocessing and up to 40 percent in inferencing, while cutting query latency by about 80 percent so end users receive near-real-time responses across commerce, care, and operations.

evidence_quotes: Amdocs is using NVIDIA DGX™ Cloud and NVIDIA AI Enterprise software to develop and deliver solutions based on commercially available large language models (LLMs) and domain-adapted models.
They’re also using NVIDIA NIM™, a set of easy-to-use inference microservices designed to accelerate the deployment of generative AI across enterprises.

Amdocs built a robust LLMOps pipeline based on the NVIDIA AI Blueprint for building data flywheels; NVIDIA NeMo™ microservices for streamlined fine-tuning, evaluation, and guardrailing; and NVIDIA NIM™ microservices.
The collaboration has successfully reduced query latency by approximately 80 percent, ensuring that end users experience near-real-time responses.
Amdocs reduced the number of tokens consumed for deployed use cases—by as much as 60 percent for data preprocessing and by up to 40 percent for inferencing.
